featured_reviews.name: ShanuKumar Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Strolling down Rani Sati Marg in Malad East, I spotted the modest yet inviting storefront of Ajay Mishtan tucked into Dwarkesh Building. Despite its small space—just seating for a handful—I felt its welcoming charm the moment I stepped inside  .

The display case was brimming with colorful sweets and snacks: golden samosas, crisp fafda, pillowy jalebis glistening in syrup. I couldn’t resist ordering a warm samosa and a couple of gulab jamuns. The samosa was delightfully crisp and savory—comfort food perfection—while the jalebis were light, sweet, and just chewy enough to bring a broad smile to my face.

I grabbed a seat on a small bench. The shop’s friendly owner nodded a greeting, and the casual chatter around—regulars sharing neighborhood news—immediately made me feel at home. There was a real sense of community in the air.

A few folks waited patiently to order, while others tapped away at their phones, eagerly anticipating takeaway boxes. I noticed how the shop balanced being a quick grab-and-go spot with a cozy breakfast corner.

With each bite, I appreciated not just the flavors but the story: the shop’s reputation for generous portion sizes yet budget-friendly pricing—about ₹200 for two, according to locals  . It felt like a place built for everyday joy, not flashy acclaim.

Leaving Ajay Mishtan, I felt satisfied—and a little nostalgic. There’s something magical about simple places like this: the crunch of a freshly fried snack, the syrupy sweetness of jalebi, and the genuine warmth of a neighborhood gem. It reminded me that happiness can often be found in the little, routine moments—especially when shared over delicious food in familiar company.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Malad's J.K. Mewawala serves only vegan sweets, making it a true gem. In Mumbai, they have three outlets; in Daman, they have one. Bring joy to you and your family this Raksha Bandhan by enjoying vegan sweets. Furthermore, they have sweets that are sugar-free. From 1974 to the present, they have served a wide variety of sweets. In addition to sweets, they also serve toffies, farsan, and dry fruits. We were very pleased with the staff's helpfulness and their explanation of each sweet in detail.

We tried:
Kaju Katli
No Added Sugar Mix Sweet
Roasted Badam Pista White Chocolate

The experience of tasting vegan sweets for the first time was enjoyable.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
MM Mithaiwala was once considered one of the go-to snack spots in its prime years — a place people would specially visit for chaat and mithai. Over time, however, it feels like it has settled into being more of a familiar, comforting neighbourhood stop rather than a standout destination. When I visited recently, it felt reliable and comforting, but not particularly memorable.

Recently tried their batata vada, samosa, and a few of the other popular dishes from the menu.

Over the years, MM has been known for its wide variety, and you’ll find almost everything here under one roof. Some popular picks worth trying include:
•	Dahi Kachori – nicely assembled with sweet and spicy chutneys, fairly typical in flavour.
•	Pani Puri & Sev Puri – good hygiene and presentation, classic sweet-tangy balance, but similar to what you’ll get at most good chaat counters across the city.
•	Khaman Dhokla – soft and fresh, mildly sweet as expected.
•	Kachori – flaky outer crust with decent stuffing, best enjoyed warm.
•	Jalebi & Fafda – especially during festive mornings, fresh and satisfying.
•	Assorted Mithai & Dryfruit Sweets – vast range, neatly displayed, standard quality.

The place remains clean and efficient, making it convenient for a quick bite or takeaway. Overall, it’s dependable and comforting, but the flavours feel quite ordinary — something you can easily find at many corners of Mumbai today.

I ordered approximately 4.5 kgs of total items and was charged ₹ 1080/- extra for delivery and the delivery address was just in range of 2 kms they are smart and cunning where they don't mention this under shipping policy but under about section.

Google should flag this listing and the details should not be of any third party entity the URL itself says it what is the google review team doing before approving the details.

featured_reviews.name: shardul mahadik
featured_reviews.review_text:
*Very disappointing experience at Bikaji, Malad West.*
We ordered Dahi Mutter Kachori, Sev Puri, and Aloo Tikki Chaat, and unfortunately all three tasted extremely sour/tangy. The balance of flavours was completely off.
The Sev Puri was the worst , it felt like extra chaat masala was added, which only increased the sourness on top of an already overly tangy tamarind chutney. It honestly makes you wonder don’t the chefs taste or check the chutneys before serving?
The food was unpleasant, inedible at some points, and a complete waste of money. What’s more upsetting is that this used to be one of our favourite places to eat out, but this experience was a total mood spoiler.
Sadly, after this visit, we won’t be coming back again.
